mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen for three consecutive weeks (-29.3 to -27.0). This momentum reflects an ongoing recovery trend in discretionary mobility that will persist, producing a higher mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days than the prior 28 days.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved from -29.3 to -27.0 over last 3 weeks
failure_condition: If the 28-day forward mean of RETAIL_REC is lower than the trailing 28-day mean despite the three-week upward trend, the momentum-continuation mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has been steadily improving (-14.6 to -12.6). If TRANSIT crosses above -10 (i.e., recovers further toward baseline), it signals increased commuting and errand trips that will pull RETAIL_REC higher within two weeks as transit-dependent shoppers resume visits.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises above -10 points from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT moved from -14.6 to -12.6 over four weeks
failure_condition: If TRANSIT crosses -10 but RETAIL_REC's next-2-week mean does not rise relative to the prior 2 weeks, the threshold mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT jointly capture commuting-linked activity. When both series rise together, combined workplace and transit recovery amplifies lunchtime and after-work retail visits beyond what either series predicts alone, raising RETAIL_REC over the next 4 weeks. The recent WORKPLACES dip (-19.9 to -22.0) combined with still-improving TRANSIT creates a mixed signal whose net interaction effect should be tested.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell from -19.9 to -22.0 in the latest week while TRANSIT kept improving
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both trend upward together but RETAIL_REC's 4-week forward mean does not exceed the trailing mean, the interaction hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL has remained persistently elevated and slightly rising (5.0 to 5.6), indicating households continue to spend more time at home than baseline. In a lockdown-relaxation plateau regime, this sustained residential elevation signals continued risk-aversion that will suppress retail and recreation visits over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose from 5.0 to 5.6 over four weeks while remaining positive throughout
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL stays elevated or rises further but RETAIL_REC's next-2-week mean still increases relative to the trailing 2 weeks, the behavioral caution hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has improved steadily (-25.9 to -22.3), consistent with seasonal warming in mid-March encouraging outdoor activity. This seasonal uptick in outdoor mobility is expected to continue independently and spill over into nearby retail visits within one week as people combine outdoor trips with shopping errands.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved from -25.9 to -22.3 over the snapshot period
failure_condition: If PARKS continues to improve but RETAIL_REC's next-week mean does not rise relative to the current week, the seasonal spillover mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has moved from negative to positive territory (-1.9 to 3.4), indicating essential-trip normalization. If GROCERY_PHARM crosses above 5 percent, it signals a behavioral threshold where households treat outings as routine again, which should quickly translate into higher RETAIL_REC within one week as the same trip-taking mindset extends to discretionary shopping.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises above 5 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose from -1.9 to 3.4 over the snapshot period
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM crosses above 5 percent but RETAIL_REC's next-week mean does not rise relative to the current week, the threshold-behavioral mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: In a regime where case counts or policy signals suggest tightening restrictions risk (not directly observed but inferable from stalled WORKPLACES recovery), any reversal of the recent mobility improvement trend across WORKPLACES and TRANSIT would presage renewed restrictions that suppress RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES declined in the latest week from -19.9 to -22.0 after three weeks of improvement
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT continue their recent stall or reversal but RETAIL_REC's 4-week forward mean still rises relative to the trailing mean, the policy-tightening hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The joint pattern of rising RESIDENTIAL and faltering WORKPLACES recovery indicates households are hedging against renewed policy restrictions by reducing non-essential outings. When both RESIDENTIAL rises and WORKPLACES simultaneously declines week-on-week, this interaction signals anticipatory caution that will depress RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks beyond what either series alone predicts.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose to 5.6 while WORKPLACES fell to -22.0 in the latest week
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL rises and WORKPLACES falls together but RETAIL_REC's next-2-week mean does not decline relative to the trailing 2 weeks, the interaction-hedging hypothesis is rejected.
